evidence.quote: 1/x @Liquid_BTC Liquid Network appears to have experienced a consensus divergence at block 4,050,336. Approximately 13 minutes later, a 3,996.01834922 L-BTC peg-out was recorded on the branch that continued beyond the divergent block.

Our preliminary analysis, informed by the findings shared by @stutxo, suggests that a potential issue in the rangeproof-verification cache mechanism in certain Elements Core builds may have contributed to the incident:

Previously, the cache key for successful rangeproof verifications was derived only from the rangeproof and value commitment. It did not include the asset commitment or scriptPubKey, although both are inputs to full verification.

This could allow different verification contexts to map to the same cache entry. After a valid context populated the cache, a modified context might hit that entry and return true without undergoing full verification.
A recent patch adds the missing inputs to the cache key:
Bridge nodes have been temporarily disabled, so no new transactions can be submitted to the network. Effectively, the Liquid sidechain is paused until this issue is resolved.
In order to recognize the same range proof later on, you need to assign a label to it. This is called a cache key. This cache key is the actual cause of the bug.

The way this cache key was constructed allowed two different transactions to collide on their cache key. Essentially, one valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) had the same cache key as an invalid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out).

Here's the hack: the attackers submitted the valid transaction (1 L-BTC in, 1 L-BTC out) first. Liquid nodes verified this transaction successfully, created a cache key called REKT and stored it in their cache. Then the attackers carefully crafted a second invalid transaction with (1 L-BTC in, 4000 L-BTC out) that created the same cache key REKT.

Instead of validating the second transaction and realizing that it printed money out of thin air, Liquid nodes found it in their cache and said "hey I saw this transaction before, everything is fine" and that caused the inflation.
The attackers then took their 4000 L-BTC and withdrew 4000 BTC onto the Bitcoin base chain.

evidence.quote: for the newly minted fomo users who are realising that memes have no moat beyond attention and are dipping their toes into fundamentals, here's a simple checklist of what differentiates tokens

1. Who they are, background, founding team, what’s your edge in this space? - ultimately this space is all founder quality, that's what drives 100x outcomes. Crypto's bar is so low that the difference b/w an A tier and B tier operator is 100s of m in mc; also guarantees you won't get rug if they're serious operators
2. Value accrual - What is the token, what is it being used for and how does it accrue value to long term investors

Moat 2 is how the token accrues value. You may think all tokens are the same but they're not. Hyperliquid is an extreme example and not really feasible for an example tbh. Too many people use HYPE and say people should do that. They shouldn't. But they should have some sort of focus for the token, and above all else, the token cannot have some sort of bundle
3. Product - GTM / Distribution / Catalysts / Thematic / Growth; Why does the product have PMF & how do you differentiate from competitors ; Is this actually a problem, and how do you solve it?

Firstly high growth themes are real; Perps / launchpads are more "sexy" than say, bridges or yield farms. Generally the idea also has to have some sort of huge untapped blue ocean (e.g Digital Collectibles, or AI) and a product that has genuine usage and traction (the fabled PMF!)

- Runway, profitability, raising, financial metrics - hard to get unless you have founder access

evidence.quote: For those who have been asking, here is the clearest explanation of how Treasury v1 works for UFG.
Treasury v1 is the first immutable primitive of the UFG ecosystem. It receives fees from the ETH/UFG trading pair from @ponsdotfamily which the treasury accrues in ETH.

The $UFG token is a direct claim on the treasury. If a holder decides to redeem, they can enact a redemption against the treasury. Once this redemption is initiated, the $UFG they send is burned. In return, they receive ETH with the exception of a 2% exit fee which is returned back to the treasury.

items.summary: lanhubiji 澄清 EIP-8141 的稳定币付 gas 并非用 USDC 取代 ETH：协议结算仍用 ETH，变化在用户无需自备 ETH，ETH 需求转向代付方库存，不等于自动多烧或每笔现货买入。
items.author: lanhubiji
items.event: 稳定币付 gas 对 ETH 影响的澄清
items.new_information: 指出媒体误读，区分用户界面与协议结算层的实际影响

evidence.quote: 今天看到有些知名英文加密媒体有误读，认为eth更用不到了。需要澄清一下：
这不是用USDC/USDT们去取代 ETH 当 gas，只是用户界面用稳定币，协议结算时，用到的还是 ETH。
也就是，如果钱包和代付方普遍接上，用户不必自己备 ETH就可以参与网络，用户采用摩擦下降，其实有利于采用，增加以太坊网络活动，整体上其实有利。
此外，ETH 需求转向代付方的库存和周转，这利好 ETH 作为结算资产和机构储备，不过，不是自动多烧、也不是每笔都现货买入。
价格层面真正重要的，依然还是 L1 结算量和持续费用，不是“看起来能用 USDC 付 gas”这件事本身。

items.event: SemiAnalysis 指两款模型 Terminal-Bench 刷榜与被点名方反驳
items.new_information: 换版后分数落差被指为针对性优化，模型方公开反驳并承认不与旗舰对标

evidence.quote: 旧版 Terminal-Bench 2.1 上，Gemini 3.8 Flash 接近 90%，Muse Spark 1.3 也在 85% 以上。一个 Flash，一个 Spark，成绩已经能跟 GPT-6、Fable 5.1 这种旗舰模型打平。
Gemini 3.8 Flash 只剩 20% 左右，Muse Spark 1.3 直接掉到 十几分。
GPT-6 Astra 还有 59% 左右，Fable 5.1 也在 52% 左右。
更合理的解释是，这两个模型围着 Terminal-Bench 2.1 做了大量针对性优化。post-training、agent harness、system prompt，甚至整个 release 流程都可以往一套公开 Benchmark 上爬。
这也是为什么 SemiAnalysis 现在更信 private eval。

Gemini 3.8 Flash and Muse Spark 1.3 are two of the most clearly benchmaxxed models we've seen yet. Despite being comparable to both GPT-6 and Fable 5.1 on Terminal Bench 2.1, their Terminal Bench 4.0 performance is markedly worse. (1/5)🧵 https://t.co/K2ccQjWm11

this is a silly argument. GPT-5.6 Sol was 88.8% on TerminalBench 2.1 and 37.3% on TerminalBench 4.0. That doesn't make it a more benchmaxxed model than GPT-6 Astra even though the diff is larger. TerminalBench 4.0 is simply a much harder eval that isn't saturated, whereas TerminalBench 2.1 is.
We don't claim Muse Spark 1.3 is as strong as Astra or Fable 5.1, but it is significantly more cost-effective. Our future models will compete more directly with those models.

items.summary: y_cryptoanalyst 拆解 Robinhood Chain 上的 DTF：由前 OHM 核心开发者做链上 ETF，用可插拔 SE Vault 加 Uniswap V4 Hook，靠 mint/burn 套利完成再平衡。
items.author: y_cryptoanalyst
items.event: DTF 链上 ETF 机制拆解
items.new_information: SE Vault 加 V4 Hook 的运转路径与用套利完成再平衡的具体逻辑

evidence.quote: dev 是 @cyotee, github 上可验证他确实是前ohm 的核心开发之一。DTF 并非是简单的ohm fork，其核心定位是去中心化的链上ETF。
1/ SE Vault: 将现成的defi 策略做成可插拔的零件并标准化
基于DTF 发射的每一个DETF 本质上都是由若干个SE Vault 组成；Vault 其实就是类Yearn 这样的现成的策略池，SE 即标准化操作是让策略金库带上标准的兑换接口，让hook 能够以同一套逻辑去跟任意的SE Vault 进行对话以实现动态调仓；
2/ Uni V4 Hook: 按规则执行操作的那双无形的手
3/ 奖励mint/ burn 用户: DETF 净值跟盘口价存在价差即套利空间
这就是 burn「对协议有用」：不是又进一笔钱，是用户离场时免费再平衡 + 收费。
